ports.note: Every layer port, on every map, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, rasterInput, polygonInput, networkInput were four separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer draws is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#drawnMode.

ontology.note: Map presentation plan and MapView activity are implemented; broader map artifact and cartographic contracts remain open. 0.11.0 declared fw:MapSpecification and the fifteen encoding properties here. That was wrong: emits records what the module named in implementation.definition asserts, and this widget is defined in src/core.ts#TYPES, which asserts nothing. The encoding terms are asserted by src/map-communication.ts and are gated by validate:ontology-coupling, which holds at zero undeclared. A release file is immutable, so 0.11.0 keeps the over-declaration and this one corrects it.

changes.description: Points carried by a polygon layer are a layer of the map: sized, coloured and shaped as Configure sets them, the same in the preview and the result, drawn over the polygons. The interactive map no longer sizes them by a column named in its code.

LINES AS A LAYER (2026-11-24). Unit tested: a polygon map draws its line layers and names them in the key; the polygon frame takes the lines in and spans the polygons alone without them; a drawn layer is marked with no setting at all and a file-sourced layer is not, 'all' marks the file layer and 'none' unmarks the drawn one, the head follows the line's direction when the line is reversed, and it is omitted where the last segment has no length; the lines port is drawable and sorts above the polygons in the layer list, named by its own step. Browser tested on Chromium: a route drawn by hand reaches the figure as two paths -- the line, and the arrowheads that carry the same layer key so a layer switched off takes them with it -- while the layer read from a GPX and the layer taken as a shared border are drawn with no arrowhead at all, which is the default rule exercised in the application rather than argued for.
